chapters.title: Two Answers, Sign by Sign
chapters.label: ch:ja-two-answers
chapters.canDo: I can write the three hiragana signs in はい and いいえ, read both answers without romanization, and say each with even mora timing.

payoff.summary: A yes-or-no choice using only three signs the learner has already traced, copied, recalled, and read.

chapters.title: A Daytime Greeting, One Sign at a Time
chapters.label: ch:ja-daytime-greeting
chapters.canDo: I can write the five distinct signs in こんにちは, read them in order, and remember why final は is pronounced wa.

payoff.summary: A one-line daytime greeting whose five signs were each taught before the learner reads it.

chapters.title: Plain Thanks, One Sign at a Time
chapters.label: ch:ja-plain-thanks
chapters.canDo: I can write and read ありがとう, build が with the dakuten, and say the five morae without swallowing the long final vowel.

payoff.summary: A plain thank-you read only after every distinct hiragana sign and the dakuten have their own small step.

chapters.title: Polite Thanks, Three More Signs
chapters.label: ch:ja-polite-thanks
chapters.canDo: I can add ございます to a known thank-you, read every sign, and choose the polite form for someone outside my close circle.

payoff.summary: A short casual-versus-polite choice with every sign taught and the register decision checked independently.

chapters.title: Nihongo, Built in Small Blocks
chapters.label: ch:ja-nihongo-kanji
chapters.canDo: I can write 日 and 本, assemble 語 from three practised components, and read 日本語 as nihongo.

payoff.summary: Three kanji read as one known word after the simple signs and the complex sign's components were taught separately.

chapters.title: Coffee in Katakana, Three Shapes
chapters.label: ch:ja-koohii-katakana
chapters.canDo: I can write コ, ー, and ヒ, read コーヒー as four morae, and explain that the long mark holds the preceding vowel.

payoff.summary: A borrowed word made from only three distinct katakana shapes, each taught before the full word appears.

chapters.title: The Doorway Exchange
chapters.label: ch:ja-doorway-exchange
chapters.canDo: I can greet, name the language, answer yes or no, and thank someone politely while listening, speaking, reading, and writing independently.

payoff.summary: A six-line doorway exchange using only words and signs already taught in the preceding six chapters.

chapters.title: One Goodbye, Sign by Sign
chapters.label: ch:ja-sayounara
chapters.canDo: I can hear and say sayōnara on five morae, write its three new hiragana signs, and read and write the complete farewell independently.

payoff.summary: A context-dependent farewell whose sound and meaning arrive before three separately taught new signs and whose payoff scores all four skills.

chapters.title: One More Time, Please
chapters.label: ch:ja-repeat-please
chapters.canDo: I can say that I do not understand, politely ask for one repetition, read and write the earned block もういちど, and write five new hiragana forms without a chart.

payoff.summary: A spoken repair assembled from independently learned pieces, with decoding and dictation limited to the signs the learner has actually earned.

chapters.title: A Little More Slowly
chapters.label: ch:ja-slower-please
chapters.canDo: I can ask for slower speech, close the repair with wakarimashita, read and write the repair lines earned in the previous chapter, and write five new hiragana signs.

payoff.summary: A second repair strategy assembled from seven tiny lexical steps while independent reading and writing stay inside the learner's earned script boundary.

chapters.title: Seven Body Words, No New Guessing
chapters.label: ch:ja-body-seven
chapters.canDo: I can read, write, hear, and say seven basic body words, and I can decode the repair signs that were previously only sound-first exposure.

payoff.summary: Seven concrete body labels built only from earned hiragana after four tiny lessons close every outstanding repair-script exposure.

chapters.title: Seven More Body Words, Spaced on Purpose
chapters.label: ch:ja-body-seven-more
chapters.canDo: I can read, write, hear, and say seven more body words while retrieving older script, greeting, farewell, and repair knowledge at expanding intervals.

payoff.summary: Seven fully decodable body labels interleaved with measured R3 and R4 retrieval rather than taught as a single topical list.
